events.title: America’s AI Chip War Is Heating Up in the Dumbest Possible Ways
events.summary: This week, the Trump administration made it significantly harder for Chinese companies to access some of the world’s most advanced AI chips. For years, tech firms like Alibaba and ByteDance could rent computing power from data centers overseas, allowing them to use powerful Nvidia chips they were generally prohibited from physically importing into China . This is known as remote access. But under new plans announced on Monday, overseas data centers that want to provide large amounts of computing power to China will have to get special licenses and deal with other annoying new kinds of red tape. The White House also imposed stricter rules on shipments of advanced chips to five countries, including Singapore and Malaysia, where US officials suspect significant levels of smuggling may have taken place. These are not new policy ideas, and similar proposals have been kicking around in Washington for a while. But the timing of Monday’s announcement is impossible to ignore. Yes, this is about Jensen Huang’s sex life. As you’ve probably heard by now, the Nvidia cofounder resigned as CEO last week after admitting he had an affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman accused of having ties to Chinese intelligence services. Alice previously worked at the Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed, which offered remote access services and is suspected of engaging in chip smuggling. The scandal may have been so embarrassing for the White House that officials felt compelled to demonstrate they had the situation under control. Apparently, the cheating scandal of the century was the motivation they were missing. (A White House spokesperson previously told WIRED that the new rule would “crack down on the smuggling of advanced US SI chips” and “help ensure that America’s most advanced chips go first to US SI innovators, not Chinese shell companies.”) It started in the fall of 2022, when the Biden administration unveiled a set of rules that would radically alter the future of AI and who was allowed to build it. The goal was to choke off China's access to the advanced chips needed to train the world's most powerful AI models, as well as the equipment required to manufacture those chips. It's worth remembering just how radical this approach was at the time. For decades, the US had used export controls to keep sensitive American technology away from specific military programs, governments, and blacklisted companies accused of carrying out human rights abuses. But the Biden administration was attempting something far more ambitious: using Washington's influence over the global semiconductor industry to hold back the world's second-largest economy from competing at the cutting edge of one of the most important new technologies in generations. The strategy rested on a relatively simple idea. Training the most advanced AI models requires enormous amounts of computing power, and American companies like Nvidia dominate the market for the chips that provide it. By restricting China's access to those chips, Washington hoped to preserve America's technological lead. Four years later, the US certainly cannot claim total victory. But boy, have things gotten messy. Part of the problem is that Washington tasked the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS), a relatively small, underfunded agency within the Commerce Department, with leading enforcement of the controls. The bureau had a budget of just $235 million in 2026—a paltry sum compared to what Nvidia rakes in in a single week. The bureau's job only got harder as the Biden administration introduced successive rounds of increasingly complex restrictions, scrambling to tighten the rules as chipmakers found increasingly elaborate ways to get around them. But one of the bureau's biggest challenges was fighting what became a booming industry for smuggling AI chips into China. At BIS, Megaspeed has become a poster child for the problem, although it's far from the only company suspected of involvement, or even the largest, according to a person familiar with the matter. According to Bloomberg, roughly 50,000 of the estimated 136,000 AI chips Megaspeed imported into Malaysia and Indonesia in 2024 and 2025 weren't accounted for in Nvidia's initial inventory checks. It's not clear where they may have ended up. (Nvidia later said it had found at least some of them.) Even if all of the unaccounted-for chips ended up in China, they would represent only a fraction of the advanced semiconductors believed to have been smuggled into the country over the past few years. Researchers at the Institute for Progress estimate that, by the end of 2026, China could have accumulated smuggled computing power equivalent to roughly 1 million of Nvidia's high-end H100 chips. But all along, Chinese companies didn't necessarily need to smuggle chips into the country to use them.

events.title: Microsoft unveils 7 AI models for coding, image editing, voice and more
events.summary: Models Transcribe Turn audio into precise transcripts Voice Generate custom voice from text Realtime Natural speech-to-speech conversations Image Generate images from text Code Fast, lightweight agentic coding Cyber Agentic defense at codebase scale Thinking Expert reasoning for complex problems Custom Models Models tuned for your needs Seven new world-class models at scalable price-performance Nov 17, 2026 · Announcements · Ignite At MAI, our mission is to build you the very best models in the world and keep every developer and every enterprise at the frontier of capability. But as token spend skyrockets, we know that you also want models at a price point that lets you run agents 24/7 doing real engineering work. That’s why today we’re releasing a family of seven new world class models at a truly exceptional price-performance. MAI Cyber 2 Flash beats GPT-6 Astra’s quality at less than 2% of the cost per task on the CyberGym-E2E benchmark. MAI Code 2 reaches 98% of the coding quality of GPT-6.1 Sol at about 40% of the price. And against Opus 5.5, it reaches 96% performance for just 5% of the price. MAI Code 2 Flash shows comparable performance GPT-6 Luna at 65% of the price, and Haiku 5.5 at 20% of the price. MAI Image 2.7 is #1 on Artificial Analysis image editing, outperforming GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst (max) at just one-fifth of the price. MAI Realtime 1 outperforms GPT-Realtime 2.1 and starts at just $0.01 per audio minute. Dragon Copilot Transcribe is built on MAI Transcribe 2, the world’s fastest and most accurate multilingual transcription model, and already powers 10 million patient encounters a month with multilingual error rates halved. Decision 1.1 is the latest decision model from Microsoft, 50x faster and 79x cheaper than GPT-6.1 Sol. Maia 200 , Microsoft’s second-generation AI accelerator, is now in production running our largest models, achieving 1.7x more tokens per watt. Frontier cyber defense built to run 24/7 Security, alignment and containment are the most important priorities for agent development in 2027 and beyond. That’s our top priority. We need to run monitoring and control agents defending and patching live production systems 24/7. That’s why MAI Cyber 2 Flash was designed to deliver frontier intelligence at a fraction of the cost. Built with Microsoft’s decades of proprietary data and world-class security expertise, our models help defenders stay safe in this new era where attackers have cheap and abundant offensive tools. MAI Cyber 2 Flash builds on earlier MAI Cyber models that defenders already rely on. MAI Cyber accounts for almost 40% of scans in MDASH, and 90% of scans that started with MAI continued to use it. Our latest model is now priced 86% lower on output tokens than MAI Cyber 1.1 Flash, giving existing MDASH customers a stronger model at a lower price. Incredible coding performance at a fraction of the cost MAI Code 2 is built for the best price-performance for everyday enterprise coding tasks. Averaged over four widely used benchmarks that target the everyday enterprise coding tasks we see in GitHub Copilot (DeepSWE 1.1, Terminal Bench 2.1, SWE-Atlas and FrontierCode v1.1), MAI Code 2 gives you 98% of the performance of GPT-6.1 Sol at 40% of the price, and 96% of Claude Opus 5.5’s performance at just 5% of the price. We’ve built these models to prioritize the coding work our customers do every day. They’re explicitly not yet tuned for harder problems, like fundamental science research and very long horizon agentic work. MAI Code 2 also been tuned to generate great dashboards and visualizations. In a blind, side-by-side evaluation of frontend work, developers preferred MAI Code 2 over GPT-6 Sol 64% of the time. Try MAI Code 2 in GitHub Copilot today. Read more here . MAI Code 2 Flash is designed for high-volume, everyday tasks like code explanations, targeted edits, routine fixes, and rapid iterations, while bringing quality at a much lower cost. It performs comparably to GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 at 65% and 20% of the price, respectively, across three coding benchmarks measuring day-to-day, high-volume routine coding tasks (DeepSWE 1.1, Terminal Bench 2.1 and SWE-Atlas). It’s available in GitHub Copilot and in a limited-access preview in Microsoft Foundry . The best image and transcription models in the world MAI Image 2.7 is the best image editing model in the world, taking the #1 spot on Artificial Analysis, outperforming GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst (max) at just one-fifth of the price. At text-to-image generation, our model is ranked #4, making us the second-best lab. And MAI Image 2.7 Flash brings world class image generation for high-volume scenarios at ~$10 per 1,000 images. Both are available in Microsoft Foundry here . MAI Realtime 1 is our first live speech-to-speech model, designed for natural, low-latency conversations. In our evaluations, it outperformed GPT-Realtime 2.1 across external and Dynamics 365 benchmarks. It’s priced for enterprise-scale use, starting at a budget-saving price of $0.01 per audio minute. You can try it out in MAI Labs and register your interest here . Dragon Copilot Transcribe , built on MAI Transcribe 2, is now live in Dragon Copilot, powering 100% of doctor–patient conversation transcriptions. It covers 10 million encounters a month, halves error rates in multilingual workflows, and is in the hands of a third of US physicians. The leading Decision model in the market Decision 1.1 provides model routing integrated right into your applications so that the bigger, pricier models are only used when you really need them. On the Artificial Analysis Decision Index Microsoft is ahead of Jev, Google and OpenAI, while being faster and cheaper. Used by 4,000 customers, it’s 50x faster and 79x cheaper than GPT-6.1 Sol. We’ve heard again and again from leaders that no one wants to pour their IQ into someone else’s model. And if you build on open weights, can you really trust where they came from, or how they’ll behave when you use one as the foundation for your most valuable IP and data? We heard you. We started with Custom Models. AT&T developed an MAI custom model for 5G network operation analytics and it outperformed GPT-6.1 Sol at 1/50th of the cost. On complex scenarios, they found that Code 2 delivered frontier-level performance at a significantly lower price than alternatives. Today, we’re taking a big step forward with MAI Licensed Weights : models under your control. Take a frontier MAI model, customize it using your proprietary data if you want to. Then run it securely in your own Azure environment. You control who can access it. Your data and adaptations stay yours. And we’ll work with you through Frontier Company to deliver the custom model and embed it in your own products and agents.

events.title: Hakeem Jeffries wins big in speaker nomination vote
events.summary: House Democrats resoundingly nominated Hakeem Jeffries for speaker Wednesday morning in a 251-11 vote. The large Democratic majority gives him plenty of wiggle room as he faces the next hurdle to becoming the first Black speaker on Jan. 3, when the full House votes. The few votes against Jeffries largely came from the progressive left of the caucus, and he’s projecting unity. “We’re going to work together to find the highest common denominator in order to make life better for the American people,” Jeffries told reporters. Rep. Lauren Underwood, D-Ill., won the day’s only contested election for vice chair in a 143-118 vote over Rep. Sara Jacobs, D-Calif. The caucus will continue elections tomorrow, with Reps. Maxwell Frost of Florida, Eric Sorensen of Illinois, Sydney Kamlager-Dove of California, and Sarah McBride of Delaware competing for three DPCC co-chair spots. Jeffries has plenty of big decisions to make now that the top leadership slate has been assembled. He’ll have to select a DCCC chair, with Reps. Steven Horsford of Nevada, Lizzie Fletcher of Texas, Brad Schneider of Illinois, and Greg Stanton of Arizona all in the mix. The caucus is also weighing whether to implement committee leadership term limits and what to do about the select committee on China and calls for a special panel on AI. — Nicholas Wu

events.title: Cyberattacks are getting faster. Here’s how Microsoft is fighting back
events.summary: Security for the agentic era, powered by Microsoft Perception A new cyber stack, built to fight AI with AI Delivering agentic security at Microsoft Ignite Changing how security work gets done A year ago, finding a serious, exploitable vulnerability was slow and expensive work done by elite security researchers. That’s no longer true. Over the past 12 months, frontier AI models have become remarkably good at discovering and exploiting software vulnerabilities, and similar levels of capability are quickly becoming available in open weights models with limited cyber guardrails. Attacks that once required specialized resources are now within reach of almost anyone. We saw what that looks like in a single week this fall when PHP disclosed two critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities, flaws that let an attacker take control of a server with a single request over the internet. 1 At the time of disclosure, tens of millions of internet-facing PHP services were running affected versions. Nearly two weeks later, about 29 million services remained vulnerable. Behind those servers are banks, healthcare providers, energy companies, and much of the infrastructure the internet runs on. And that same day brought five other major disclosures across the industry. Turning a flaw like the PHP one into a working attack once took a specialist team months. Within roughly a day of PHP2Shell’s disclosure, security researchers had developed a working, weaponized exploit. By the following week, that research had expanded to cover additional PHP versions and configurations. The time from discovery to exploit is shrinking from months to minutes. The physics of cybersecurity are changing, and fast. AI is amplifying risk. Attackers can now find and exploit gaps faster than defenders can close them. Attacks are becoming fully automated. AI has moved from assisting attackers, to executing their tasks, to planning and running entire campaigns on its own. Agents are the new insiders. While not inherently malicious, they perform tasks and business workflows at machine speed, around the clock, and have broad access to data, apps, tools, and other agents. Like any insider, they can make mistakes, be manipulated, or be compromised. What we built for humans does not scale for AI. Frontier Transformation starts with business outcomes and a simple idea: technology was invented to serve humanity, not the other way around. To help organizations bring their ideas to life and innovate safely in the agentic era, we need a new cyber stack, built for agentic security. The Microsoft cyber stack has three layers: Signals, sensors, and actuators . This foundational layer is powered by sensors and actuators in Microsoft Defender, Microsoft Entra, Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Sentinel, the network, the operating system, the browser, and our hyperscale cloud. Sensors tell you something is wrong. Actuators let you do something about it: contain a device on the network, revoke an identity’s access, or block an agent at the authorization layer. And because we know we’re not the only security solution provider in your environment, we connect to the wider ecosystem through more than 500 connectors. Together, Microsoft and partner sources produce more than 165 trillion signals a day, 2 which, enriched by Microsoft and customer threat intelligence, fuel the context layer. Context . This layer organizes those signals, together with each customer’s own environment, into agent-ready, real-time understanding of the digital estate that is optimized for precision, recall, and token efficiency. Agents, harness, and models . On top are specialized security agents that work together as teams through playbooks, directed by a harness, and a multi-model approach that uses the right model for each task, designed to ensure effective and efficient security outcomes, at scale. At Microsoft Ignite 2026 , we’re delivering innovation across every layer of the stack. It starts with Microsoft Perception , now generally available . Perception brings the top of the stack together. It orchestrates red, blue, and green team agents through playbooks, working together in a closed loop to deliver security outcomes. Red team agents simulate attacks from an attacker’s perspective before a breach occurs. Blue team agents detect, triage alerts, and investigate attacks, freeing analysts to focus on the critical decisions that matter most. Green team agents fix and remediate. Perception is built to help security teams move at machine speed, drive outcomes rather than tasks, and automate while staying in control. Your team sets the guardrails and signs off on high-impact actions, and automated triggers launch playbooks when an incident meets the criteria you set. New cost management dashboards and a cost estimator help you track AI usage, forecast spending, and connect costs to measurable security outcomes. Agents are only as good as what they can see and what they can do. That’s why we are investing as much in the foundation as in the layers above it. Integrated Security Operations Center (ISOC) in Microsoft Defender , generally available for core capabilities , is part of that foundation. ISOC brings security information and event management (SIEM) capabilities, user and entity behavior analytics (UEBA), threat intelligence, and threat protection and disruption together so you can start your journey to the agentic security operations center (SOC). Eligible Defender Suite, Microsoft 365 E5, and Microsoft 365 E7 customers receive all Microsoft Sentinel SIEM features, 90-day default data retention for Defender data, more than 500 connectors, reduced ingestion rates, and a built-in data lake. The complete breadth of SIEM capabilities is now in preview. Read on to learn how Microsoft Perception, ISOC in Defender, and new capabilities across the stack work together to help customers secure their foundations, secure agentic insiders, and defend with agents. Defending against AI-speed attacks starts with closing the doors attackers walk through first, and the scale of that work is increasing. In 2026, more than 96,000 vulnerabilities 3 have been published to the CVE (Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures) Program, more than double 2024’s roughly 40,000 and more than 20 times the level of 2010, 4 driven in part by AI-assisted vulnerability discovery tools. Yet only 26% of vulnerabilities in the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog were remediated in 2025, as remediation typically extends into weeks and months. AI finds those gaps faster than teams can close them. Today we’re announcing new capabilities to help. Strengthen your security foundation with Perception .

events.title: Islam will overtake Christianity as world's largest religion by 2035: Pew
events.summary: Data: Pew Research ; Chart: Erin Davis/Axios Islam is expected to surpass Christianity as the world's largest religion by 2035, according to Pew Research Center projections released Wednesday. Why it matters: The shift has less to do with people converting to Islam and more to do with who's having more kiddos , a demographic trend poised to reshape the world's religious makeup as Christianity's center of gravity moves to Africa. By the numbers: Muslims are projected to gain 1.6 billion people through births exceeding deaths from 2020 to 2070, according to new Pew data released Wednesday. Christians are expected to gain 792 million people through natural population change. From 2020 to 2025, Muslim women had an average fertility rate of 3.1 children, compared with 2.5 for Christian women. For all other women, the average was 1.6. What they're saying: "These religious figures are driven by demographic change," David Voas, a University College London professor who researches secularization, tells Axios. He says the countries growing the fastest — in North Africa, the Middle East, Near East and South Asia — have a relatively high Muslim population, so naturally Islam would eventually be the most populous religion. Zoom in: The U.S. is expected to lose more Christians than any other country by 2070, even as Christianity grows globally. The U.S. had the world's largest Christian population in 2020, at 217 million. By 2070, that number is expected to drop to 174 million. Meanwhile, the Democratic Republic of the Congo is expected to have nearly 300 million Christians by 2070, far surpassing the U.S. By then, 54% of the world's Christians are projected to live in sub-Saharan Africa. "The center of gravity of Christianity has been shifting towards the global south," Voas says. "Traditionally, we tended to think of Christianity as being a kind of Western religion … but of course Christianity was taken to Africa and around the world, and Africa is now growing faster than anywhere else." Between the lines: Both Christianity and Islam are expected to lose more followers than they gain through religious switching, including people leaving religion entirely. But Christianity's losses will be far larger. Zoom out: Islam becoming the world's largest religion doesn't necessarily mean a dramatic shift in global political or cultural power, Voas says. "I would not see any major change in the balance of either political or cultural power, at least in the medium term," he said, adding that it's possible some will assimilate to the local culture and expectations. "There's some wild talk about Europe being taken over by Muslims and so on. That is not going to happen in any foreseeable future." The bottom line: Islam may soon claim the top spot, but the numbers don't necessarily translate into a seismic shift in global influence. events.title: Trust, but prepare: How to make sense of AI's age of upheaval
events.summary: Most Americans are baffled and alarmed by the daily, if not hourly, explosion of technical glitches hitting air travel, banks and work products like Microsoft Outlook. The outages seem genuinely scary and related. So what the hell is going on? The most likely answer : This is the first true wave of unintended consequences of increasingly powerful artificial intelligence hitting us at once. The big picture: In short, AI is exceptionally good at building software, and therefore exceptionally good at spotting and exploiting bugs in large technical, software-based systems. The glitches come from a mix of sources — some innocuous, some scary, including: routine updates to aging infrastructure; humans scrambling to patch vulnerabilities discovered by AI; hackers exploiting existing weaknesses; and bad actors using swarms of AI agents to launch increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks. That's the new reality that government officials and AI experts believe we're entering. They expect this period of disruption and heightened vulnerability to persist for months, as powerful new AI tools expose weaknesses buried in decades-old systems. The catchphrase gaining currency : " Software Beirut " — a period of cascading failures, many of our own making, that could grow worse before things get better. What this means for YOU : Understand the different causes, detailed below, and resist the temptation to panic every time something goes haywire. It's easy to hop on social media and let the algorithm drag you into doomsday thinking. You should also prepare : Reset and protect your passwords . Keep more cash on hand if possible, in case your bank is down for a day or two. Buy some basic emergency supplies in case power or water do go out. Sadly, we believe this season of glitches and possible cyberattacks will persist. Better to be prepared. Here's a more detailed look at the different causes of these glitches or breakdowns: 1. Updates to old systems: The government says last Friday's nationwide airspace outage was simply a case of replacing old copper wires with new fiber that went very, very badly. Aging infrastructure can struggle to accommodate new components. In this case, a network problem overwhelmed legacy equipment, triggering a cascade that grounded flights across the country. 2. AI spotting bugs and humans rushing to fix them: This is one of cyber expert Nicole Perlroth's core scenarios, which went viral this week. AI can find vulnerabilities faster than humans can investigate and patch them. In the frantic sprint to fix those weaknesses before hackers exploit them, systems can break. According to the Washington Sun , banking executives and NSA officials have told lawmakers that rushed efforts to patch AI-discovered vulnerabilities contributed to some of this week's outages. 3. Bad actors attacking vulnerable systems : Across Europe, supermarket refrigerators are being hacked , spoiling millions of dollars' worth of food. No one had "protect the fridges" on their security to-do list this year. But the attacks show how hackers can exploit even the most mundane internet-connected systems — with devastating real-world consequences. 4. AI enabling new forms of cyberattacks : Google said this week it had identified, for the first time, bad actors using AI to find weaknesses and launch cyberattacks entirely on their own — with no human in the loop. If it wasn't already clear, Google warned that "the adversarial AI landscape has reached a critical inflection point." The bottom line: Most companies and much of government are woefully unprepared for the new era of AI-powered cyberattacks. Their systems are old, clunky and riddled with vulnerabilities. Fortifying them will take enormous amounts of money, time and persistence. The good news: We can see the danger coming, and still have (a little) time to protect ourselves for what may come next. Axios' Ben Berkowitz and Zachary Basu contributed.

events.title: The senators who could join Van Hollen's insurgency against Schumer
events.summary: Sen. Chris Van Hollen is picking up endorsements in his challenge to Chuck Schumer for Senate Democratic leader. Why it matters: The leadership fight exposes divisions within the Democratic Party days after its sweeping midterm victory , with some demanding a new direction and others crediting Schumer for the historic blue wave. Driving the news: Van Hollen (D-Md.), a senator since 2017, announced Thursday he's challenging Schumer because "we need new leadership." "This is not about any one person — it's about answering the call of the American people." The other side: Schumer has far more public endorsements than Van Hollen. "Why would you fire the manager when you just won the World Series?" Sen. Angus King (I-Maine) said in a statement of support for Schumer. Van Hollen has disputed Schumer's claim to credit for the party's midterm performance, arguing that the wave was powered by voters rather than leaders in Washington. By the numbers: Schumer has public support from 14 senators, including himself, compared with five for Van Hollen. A candidate will need 28 or 29 votes to win, depending on the outcome of Alaska's Senate race, where votes are still being counted. Senators backing Van Hollen State of play: Van Hollen told MS NOW he has "more than 10" senators on his side, though only four have publicly endorsed him. Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) endorsed Van Hollen on Thursday night, saying he will fight for working families. Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed (D-Mich.) threw his support behind Van Hollen when he announced his challenge Thursday. Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.) issued an endorsement for Van Hollen Friday afternoon. Incoming Sen. Peggy Flanagan (D-Minn.) endorsed Van Hollen Friday morning after previously calling for new leadership. Who wants new leadership? Some sitting senators have called for a leadership change without endorsing Van Hollen. Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.) has called for change but hasn't endorsed either candidate. Before Van Hollen announced his candidacy, Sen. Peter Welch (D-Vt.) told NBC 5 Democrats "absolutely are committed to change," but didn't rule out supporting Schumer. Several Democratic senators-elect have also called for new leadership: Sen.-elect Adam Hamilton (D-Kan.). Sen.-elect Juliana Stratton (D-Ill.). Sen.-elect Troy Jackson (D-Maine). Sen.-elect Annie Andrews (D-S.C.). Sen.-elect Chris Pappas (D-N.H.). Context: Progressive critics say Schumer hasn't fought hard enough against President Trump and his agenda. Schumer's decision to help advance a Republican-backed government funding bill in March 2025 fueled the progressive backlash against his leadership. The progressive Working Families Party urged Schumer "not to seek another term as Senate Democratic Leader" in a letter, as first reported by Axios . Another labor group has also opposed Schumer and endorsed Van Hollen. Who's backing Schumer? Schumer entered the leadership fight with broad support among Senate Democrats. "I have the votes to continue serving as Democratic leader," Schumer (D-N.Y.) said in a statement this week. Schumer's public supporters include Sen.-elect Sherrod Brown (D-Ohio), Sens. Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), John Fetterman (D-Pa.) and King , along with Schumer himself. Also backing Schumer: Sens. Sheldon Whitehouse (R.I.), Ruben Gallego (Ariz.), Mark Kelly (Ariz.), Richard Blumenthal (Conn.), Brian Schatz (Hawaii), Catherine Cortez Masto (Nev.), Jacky Rosen (Nev.), Tammy Baldwin (Wis.) and Jack Reed (R.I.). Schumer also received pre-election endorsements from Sen. Tim Kaine (D-Va.) and Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.). Alsobrooks declared full support for Schumer on Wednesday, but Kaine has yet to publicly reaffirm his support. Senators who haven't picked a side Several sitting senators have yet to publicly back either candidate. Sen. Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.), Sen. Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Sen. Mark Warner (D-Va.) and Sen. Patty Murray (D-Wash.) have not publicly committed to either candidate. Sen. Andy Kim (D-N.J.) and Sen. Chris Coons (D-Del.) have called for a caucus debate over leadership. Sens. Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.) and Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.) have expressed openness to a leadership change without endorsing either candidate. Sen.-elect James Talarico (D-Texas) hasn't committed to Schumer and wants to hear his vision for the Senate. The 2028 factor Several potential 2028 presidential contenders face a choice over who should lead Senate Democrats. Ossoff and Booker , both possible 2028 presidential contenders, have yet to pick sides — leaving them to choose between the party's longtime leader and a changing of the guard. Meanwhile, Gallego and Kelly , also seen as possible 2028 contenders, have backed Schumer. Zoom out: Schumer himself is up for reelection in 2028 and could face a primary challenge from Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez (D-N.Y.), who has also been mentioned as a potential presidential contender. Schumer could also retire rather than seek reelection . What's next: Senate Democrats will hold a secret-ballot leadership election Dec. 1. Incoming senators will participate, and members can cast their ballots differently from their public endorsements. events.title: Tech leaders see silver lining in data center backlash
events.summary: Maybe a slowdown of the AI buildout is… actually a good thing for the AI industry. Some global tech leaders at Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World suggested that backlash to data centers or a potential financing bubble might provide the necessary brakes that the industry needs. A reset could mean businesses get a moment to catch up on grid capacity, fiber connectivity, cybersecurity, and to sweeten the deals data-center developers bring to communities where they’re building. Mubadala CEO Khaldoon Al Mubarak acknowledged that winter is coming for the AI buildout and broader economy, but said “ winter doesn’t mean minus 30 degrees. It could be a nice pleasant winter. ” One AI executive said companies must do a better job of messaging how much energy and water data centers actually consume (in one case, a useful example has been telling people data centers are less wasteful than playing a round of golf); another said AI companies need to be more aware of how “violent” it can be when they enter a community and start sucking up resources. Tech executives were reflecting on AI backlash in Silicon Valley, but stopping the buildout altogether? Not a chance. — J.D. Capelouto and Ashley Gold

events.title: Build a Personal Brand to Help Employers Find You
events.summary: This article is crossposted from IEEE Spectrum ’s careers newsletter. Sign up now to get insider tips, expert advice, and practical strategies, written i n partnership with tech career development company Parsity and delivered to your inbox for free! In one year, the number of developers working for themselves has more than doubled. Stack Overflow’s annual survey of more than 30,000 developers showed that freelancers and sole proprietors went from about four percent of respondents to ten percent. You can read this as a polite way of saying, “ I got laid off and I’m figuring it out.” But I don’t think the number can be ignored. Whatever the case, it leads to the question I keep hearing from engineers right now: What can I do to stay employable? One tried and true answer is to build a personal brand. But what does that actually mean? Over the last six years, I grew my LinkedIn audience to 40,000 followers and YouTube channel to 10,000. I don’t think you should aim to be famous (unless you’re into that sort of thing) but I do think it’s worth exploring how to be discoverable online in 2027 if you want an advantage in the open market. A personal brand is a discovery mechanism Strip away the follower counts and the AI-generated thought leadership, and a personal brand comes down to a simple question: Does the internet know who you are? When a hiring manager goes looking for someone who has your skills, do you show up? You can think of this as search engine optimization for your employability. Recruiters have mostly consolidated around a single platform to find people: LinkedIn. Those 40,000 followers and millions of impressions came with barely a viral post to my name. Nobody is begging me to do sponsorships. But I rarely have trouble finding work, and far more opportunities come to me than I go looking for. That has much less to do with fame than with being easy to find. You don’t need 10,000 followers. You need a trail of breadcrumbs. Don’t write AI slop LinkedIn is notorious for being overrun with AI-generated posts. It’s become a running joke. That’s good news for you, because the bar to stand out is “sound like a human being.” Write about what you actually achieved: a hairy bug you squashed, how your team handles deployments, why you picked some obscure library, the migration that went sideways at 2 a.m. Specifics are hard to fake and easy to trust. (But be careful not to post sensitive information.) And post a picture of yourself once in a while. People connect with faces a lot faster than with walls of text. Hot takes, with caution Posts with an opinion tend to outperform tutorials, but you don’t have to dunk on anyone to have one. For instance, if you work on a tech stack people love to mock (VB, .NET, some ancient Java monolith held together with prayer), try something like “What people get wrong about .NET.” You’ll attract a few trolls in the comments—free engagement, honestly—plus people who want an actual conversation. These comments can turn into actual connections and even… friends. A routine you can follow Posting twice a week is not a big ask. Pick a simple, repeatable format so you’re never staring at an empty text box: what you worked on, what broke, and what you learned. Even a post that gets 10 views leaves one more breadcrumb about who you are and what you know. Over time, the people who comment become your network. And because so few engineers post about their work on LinkedIn, you can become a big fish in a small pond surprisingly fast. Write for the people a few steps behind you The best audience is engineers one or two steps behind where you are now. Answer the questions you had a year ago. It helps them, it sharpens your own thinking, and every so often it turns into mentorship in both directions. It also tells a future employer more about how you think than any résumé bullet ever could. The engineers who grab the most opportunities are the ones employers can find. You don’t need to become an influencer to be one of them. You just need to leave enough breadcrumbs that the right person can follow them back to you. —Brian IEEE Xplore Digital Library Adds AI Assistant To help researchers search through the millions of peer-review publications in the IEEE Xplore Digital Library, IEEE has released a custom AI suite optimized for STEM literature. The suit allows users to search with natural-language queries and provides overviews with reference links. Read more here . events.title: Inside Nvidia’s First Post-Jensen All-Hands: Pay Raises and More Equity
events.summary: Interim Nvidia CEO Colette Kress made her first address to the staff on Wednesday and just minutes into the meeting told employees that they can expect pay raises and more equity in December, months ahead of schedule, according to remarks reviewed by WIRED. “So I’m here to tell you, the best thing that we want to do is to take care of each and every single employee that is here and to make sure that you feel good about this company and you do not worry about your comp,” she said. Questions about compensation were the most common among the 700 submitted ahead of the meeting, Kress said. She said the next-most common request was for transparency from the board. Kress’ comments came during the first companywide meeting following the resignation of Jensen Huang as CEO last week. Huang had led the computer graphics chip maker since cofounding it 33 years ago, and his presentations during the quarterly town halls internally had become a much anticipated and memorable spectacle for some of the company’s nearly 49,000 employees. Information rarely leaked from the meetings in the past. Nvidia declined to comment for this story. But now Nvidia is facing an extraordinary leadership crisis . Huang resigned amid allegations of extramarital affairs, including potentially with a Chinese intelligence asset. Nvidia’s board chair Harvey Jones said on Tuesday that Huang disclosed “personal behavior” contrary to the company’s policies and norms and wouldn’t be invited back. During the companywide meeting on Wednesday, Jones reiterated that the board accepted Huang’s resignation due to his personal conduct and “lack of candor.” He said the company wouldn’t find a “Jensen clone,” but that there are “dynamic leaders out there, with demonstrated intellect, high-tech engineering experience, strategic thinking, cultural compatibility, and a track record of success.” He added, “We will not compromise our requirements for the sake of expediency” and that the board would accept employee suggestions on the CEO search. Thousands of employees have apparently lobbied for Huang’s reinstatement. Several well-known tech executives signed a public petition, with about 200,000 purported backers urging the same. Instead, the board is searching internally and externally for a replacement at one of the world’s most valuable companies and one of the biggest drivers of the generative AI boom. Huang’s departures and a slew of government investigations into him and Nvidia have rattled investors. But on Tuesday, Nvidia reported better-than-expected financial results and forecast growing sales in the years to come. Shares were up about 5 percent on Wednesday. One concern investors have expressed is whether Nvidia might see a brain drain of top talent. Many employees have stayed at Nvidia for Huang and his vision. Nvidia could also be perceived as a less desirable place for new and emerging talent to work, with its leadership in flux, during an especially critical time as competition in the AI chips market grows. On Tuesday’s third-quarter earnings call, an analyst from Bank of America Securities asked Kress directly about her “message” to Nvidia investors about talent retention, as well as the company’s overall durability and financial strategy through this major upheaval. Kress replied that “probably the most important thing” company leaders are thinking through right now is stabilizing its employee ranks. “We are always thinking about our employees. Like every community out there, there are diverse opinions,” Kress said. “We will take care of our employees during this transition to make sure they are safe and make sure the work can be done in the current environment.” In a brief question-and-answer session with Kress during the all-hands meeting Wednesday, Nvidia cofounder Chris Malachowsky addressed how the company could maintain its prized culture going forward. He recalled how he, Huang, and other cofounders thought it was “nonsense” to put cultural values up on posters. Instead, they want it instilled in “the way you behave, the way you work together, and the way you work,” and he believes that will stand the test of time. “We’re going to be fine,” he said. Kress ended the meeting, which lasted about 50 minutes, by comparing Nvidia’s employees to “90,000 people packed into the sweatiest, hottest” University of Florida football game. In the third quarter, “every single person sings,” she said. “It is impressive to see them all together, all in harmony singing that song … Do you know what? We’re gonna hear that song, guys. And I believe in all of you, that you will help sing it. Nvidia, we’ve got this.” Updated: 11/18/2026 1:26 p.m. EST: Updated with new details on comments made during the Nvidia all-hands meeting. events.title: Microsoft and Intel deepen collaboration to deliver differentiated Azure infrastructure
events.summary: November 18, 2026 Category: Company News Microsoft and Intel deepen collaboration to deliver differentiated Azure infrastructure The two companies are working together to develop differentiated capabilities in Azure and system-level optimizations, tailoring infrastructure to the performance, efficiency, scalability and security requirements of cloud and AI Microsoft Source | 4 minutes REDMOND, Wash., and SANTA CLARA, Calif. – November 17, 2026 — Microsoft (Nasdaq: MSFT) and Intel (Nasdaq: INTC) today announced an expansion of their decades-long collaboration under a long-term agreement to advance select areas of Azure infrastructure for growing cloud and AI demand. Microsoft is the first company to announce use of Intel Foundry’s EMIB (Embedded Multi-die Interconnect Bridge) advanced packaging technology for Azure first-party silicon. Bringing together Intel silicon and EMIB capabilities with Microsoft’s cloud engineering, the agreement confirms multi-year Intel® Xeon® supply capacity – including instances of next generation server CPUs, codenamed Diamond Rapids – and expands collaboration across the Azure roadmap and Intel-based Azure hardware systems. Microsoft will also collaborate with Intel on Intel Xeon with Compute Express Link (CXL) to drive greater memory efficiency and system-level innovation across Azure, as well as Intel QuickAssist (Intel QAT) and confidential computing. This work further advances existing memory and database performance, including: Up to 2.3x greater performance 1 and memory flexibility for demanding workloads in Azure M-series v4 virtual machines with CXL memory and Intel Flat Memory Mode in Xeon 6 processors. Improved performance and reliability with up to 2.5x faster SQL backups 2 on Azure through the first Intel QuickAssist Technology (QAT) enabled virtual machines in the cloud. Virtual machine memory and CPU register state encryption as confidential VMs move between hosts through Intel Trust Domain Extensions (Intel TDX). Together, these investments are designed to provide Microsoft customers a more predictable, scalable and resilient infrastructure foundation, with compute optimized for demanding cloud and AI workloads, more efficient memory and stronger capabilities for protecting sensitive workloads. “Our customers need infrastructure built around the workloads that matter to them. Our longstanding collaboration with Intel brings together advanced packaging, custom compute, memory and security capabilities to support Azure compute and continued innovation across Azure. Together, we are connecting silicon and systems engineering to move the industry forward and meet the growing demand for Cloud + AI computing for our customers,” said Saurabh Dighe, CVP, Azure System & Architecture, Microsoft. “Microsoft and Intel share a clear view of where AI infrastructure is headed–increasingly complex systems designed through the co-optimization of silicon, packaging, compute memory and software,” said Naga Chandrasekaran, EVP, Chief Technology and Operations Officer and General Manager of Intel Foundry. “Through use of our advanced packaging capabilities with EMIB to scale future generations of Azure infrastructure, Intel and Microsoft can combine the flexibility of heterogeneous integration with the manufacturing scale required for the AI era—giving customers new levels of performance and economics when interacting with Azure.” About Microsoft Microsoft enables digital transformation for the era of an intelligent cloud and an intelligent edge. events.title: House Democrats formally nominate Hakeem Jeffries for speaker
events.summary: House Democrats voted at a closed-door caucus meeting Wednesday morning to nominate Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) as their candidate for speaker. Why it matters: It's a symbolic but significant step that suggests Jeffries has the votes he needs to be elected the first Black House speaker on Jan. 3. Jeffries won 251 of the 262 votes cast, putting him comfortably above the 218 votes he needs to win on the House floor in January. The vote was tallied at Jeffries' request . His allied had initially hoped he would be elected by acclamation, but the Democratic leader changed tack at the 11th hour and decided to call his detractors' bluff. Between the lines: Wednesday's caucus vote was a secret ballot. On Jan. 3, each House member will have to stand up during a televised proceeding and announce who they are voting for. That could be difficult for the members — particularly progressives — who have been flooded with calls and emails from constituents urging them not to vote for him. Only a handful of incoming House members, including Reps.-elect Angela Gonzales-Torres (D-Calif.) and Don Leonard (D-Ohio), have outright said they will oppose Jeffries thus far.

events.title: Democrats turn the page on Biden
events.summary: David’s view The Federal Aviation Administration meltdown that stranded many Democrats in Denver last weekend highlighted a grand political irony. Former President Joe Biden gave his life to a political party that doesn’t want to think about him. Donald Trump’s Republicans want people to keep Biden on their minds. “The Biden Administration was an FAA disaster,” Trump wrote on Truth Social, as the airlines slowly recovered from their forced grounding. Asked for contrition, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said he took “responsibility for what was given to me by prior administrations.” Blaming Biden for problems that haven’t been fixed since he returned to Delaware comes easy to this White House. In Denver, where Democrats gathered to take a midterm victory lap while looking ahead to 2028, the Biden years were mentioned rarely, usually in sweeping statements about how Democrats shouldn’t just restore the country to what was before Trump. “Capitalism in America now is fundamentally broken for most people,” said Gina Raimondo, Biden’s secretary of commerce for four years. They wouldn’t trash the guy, but the idea that he could have “restored the soul of America” and banished MAGA felt a little embarrassing. I didn’t hear any Democrat get asked about , Biden’s third memoir, which arrived this week to scathing reviews. This isn’t another one of those reviews, though the book is a real chore to get through. (Get hyped for sentences like this: “My audience in the State Department auditorium responded with generous applause.“) Biden remains one of the last men in America who believes that he could have won the 2024 election. It was the “pundits,” not a majority of voters, who decided by mid-2023 that he was too old to continue in the job. Early in the memoir, reflecting on how he was ready to win the presidency on his third try, Biden paraphrases Heraclitus on how “a man cannot step in the same river twice.” If you see the inconsistency between that and the insistence that only the man who had beaten Trump once could beat him again, then you are not Joe Biden. “I could have fought to the convention,” Biden writes. “Taken the fight to the floor. Forced a vote. And probably prevailed.” He ruminates over how he won more votes as a write-in candidate in New Hampshire than Trump won in a contested primary: “I was supposed to be LBJ in 1968. Run out of the race.” This is old news. Democrats now agree that Biden was selfish to seek a new term in his 80s. What is the legacy of his one term? That’s much more contested. The former president is still proud that he fended off the “uncommitted” movement that denied him primary voters in a protest of his support for Israel’s war in Gaza. That was a tribute to his leadership. The collapse of Democratic support for the war since he left office can be blamed on Benjamin Netanyahu, not him. “I hope Israel wakes up,” Biden writes. “The days of American leaders like me — passionate defenders of Israel to the core — are passing.” He has less to say about a cause adopted during 2020 — leading America through a “racial reckoning” after the murder of George Floyd. Biden recounts that he signed 17 executive orders on his first day as president, but only focuses on five of them, related to climate, COVID-19, immigration, and the economy. There’s no mention of his order for a “comprehensive approach to advancing equity for all, including people of color and others who have been historically underserved.” The word “equity” doesn’t appear in the memoir. Biden argues instead that “every one of my legislative accomplishments had justice baked in,” including “equal access to vaccines.” In the words of Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, D-NY, whom Biden repeatedly thanks for supporting him when other Democrats wanted to end his campaign: Woke one was crazy. Gender gets the same treatment. Biden, who had called anti-transgender discrimination “the civil rights issue of our time,” never uses the word “transgender” in his memoir. He doesn’t mention his Day 1 executive order that banned discrimination on the basis of gender identity. Rachel Levine, the first transgender American confirmed to an executive branch position by the Senate, doesn’t appear in the book. Sarah McBride, D-Del., the first transgender American elected to Congress and a longtime Biden ally, is mentioned only in a list of winners he called on election night in 2024. You could read this as an endorsement of McBride’s political strategy , which acknowledges the backlash to the LGBTQ+ rights movement and makes Republicans the culture war aggressors. Biden, who did prove his doubters wrong by finally winning the presidency in 2020, did so with a progressive agenda and focus that was hard to identify in his pre-2020 career. Biden doesn’t say that his party lost chances to build broader support and prevent a Trump comeback by going too far to the left. You just figure that out for yourself, between the bits about the party and the people not appreciating him enough. He now says that he rescued the country, not that he tried to transform it. “Far from an open-border policy, I kept in place the cornerstone of the Trump border and immigration policy for most of my presidency,” Biden writes. The high-flying promises of 2020, like a “surge” of asylum seekers denied entry to the country by Trump, are not here. What does Biden think of Trump rolling back temporary protected status for Haitian refugees? He doesn’t mention his expansion of the Temporary Protected Status program at all. The next Democratic primary, well underway already, begins with the assumption that it made too many mistakes in 2020. The tougher internal debate is about the mistakes made after it united behind Biden, and beat Trump. We now know what Biden thinks about that, and his role in the process is over. Notable In The Atlantic, long-time Biden reporter Matt Viser reviewed the memoir and reflected on what Biden doesn’t acknowledge: “If he had run in 2024 and won, he would now be a visibly frail 83-year-old man, fighting a vicious form of cancer.”

events.title: Tech leaders form tribal loyalties after Huang ouster
events.summary: Liz’s view One former politico-turned-tech executive who had just come from Washington told me this week: “Out here, the question is whether Jensen will be back at Nvidia by Christmas or whether it’ll take a little longer. In Washington, it’s whether he’s going to prison.” Huang does not currently face criminal charges, and it’s still unclear what he knew about Alice Huang’s alleged connections to Chinese intelligence. But that’s the gulf between DC and Silicon Valley right now, one we tried to bridge this week through tough interviews with people on both sides. We surely didn’t close it, but two things cleared up as the rain clouds moved out of Menlo Park. Tech executives, even those pushing to bring Huang back, have been chastened by the one-two punch of his downfall and the blue sweep in the midterm elections. And Washington is tired of their arrogance, or at least keenly aware that voters are. “What [people are] really against is this feeling that, ‘man, are the people building AI actually, really, truly on Team Human?’” said OpenAI’s Sam Altman, who did not sound like a CEO excited to go public even as his main rival, Anthropic, lists as soon as tomorrow. Even the #SaveJensen crowd at the top of Sand Hill Road was subdued. Bill Ackman, one of the first to rush to Huang’s defense, all but said he’d fire a CEO who lied to him as a board member. Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas said the US “ needs more Jensens ” but demurred when asked if Huang should return to Nvidia. Jeff Bezos thinks the job should go to an insider: “Outside CEOs in a complex company have a vanishingly small chance of succeeding.” Notable Many tech leaders are openly pushing for Huang’s return to Nvidia: A petition with more than 175,000 signatures calling for the Nvidia board to reinstate him includes Uber cofounder Travis Kalanick and Elon Musk as signatories.

events.title: ‘Just Ridiculous’: A Famed Philosopher Takes on AI Consciousness
events.summary: Over 50 years ago, philosopher Thomas Nagel asked the question, “What Is It Like to Be a Bat?” The question opened up an examination on whether people could understand the consciousness of nonhumans and the meaning of consciousness itself. Who knew that, a half- century later, the question would move from an ivory-tower rumination to a critical issue in the future of humanity as we try to make sense of disturbingly sentient-adjacent chatbots ? The paper became a classic and it helped set a foundation for a career that saw Nagel make contributions to thought on morality, justice, and the mind-body question. One of his books is titled What Does It All Mean? For the breadth and quality of his work, he became the recipient this week of the $1 million Berggruen Prize for Philosophy & Culture , given annually to “an individual whose ideas have profoundly shaped human self-understanding and advancement in a rapidly changing world.” Previous winners include Peter Singer and Ruth Bader Ginsburg. I used the occasion to speak to Nagel at his home in Greenwich Village, New York, specifically to hear about how the evolution of artificial intelligence might have affected his viewpoint. It turns out that the 89-year-old professor emeritus at NYU had given the question a lot of thought and had some strong views on the subject. The interview is edited for clarity and length. WIRED: It’s been 52 years since you wrote “What Is It Like to Be a Bat?,” which has become an iconic paper about understanding consciousness in non-humans. Has the emergence of large language models altered your thinking? THOMAS NAGEL: Like everyone, I’m tremendously impressed by the lifelikeness of these systems compared to the history of earlier AI . But the disposition of some philosophers to take seriously the question whether these things are conscious or might soon become conscious is just ridiculous. They are assuming that the physical substrate is irrelevant. They all think that the material conditions for consciousness can be given in functionalist terms. For those of us who have forgotten our philosophy classes, tell us about functionalism. Functionalism is substrate-independent. It’s more than likely that the truth is one which links physical processes and systems of certain kinds to mental phenomena. Complicated data centers have absolutely nothing in common with the physical character of a nervous system. We have strong reasons to believe that while there may be consciousness elsewhere in the universe, it would require the appearance of some kind of organism with something analogous to a nervous system. But isn’t all consciousness subjective? Just like we don’t know what it’s like to be a bat, we don’t know what it feels like to be a large language model. Bats are conscious. We just don’t have the imaginative capacity to form a conception of the aspects of that subjectivity that depend on echolocation. It would be radically unscientific to conclude that bats are not conscious from the fact that we can’t imagine what it’s like, but in the case of AI, there is a very simple reason that the supposition that they might be conscious is ridiculous. All they produce is language, and language by itself is not a natural manifestation of consciousness. I apologize for being too exercised about this. This is a very distressing situation to me. What if you have a robot body? Isn’t that a substrate? I don’t exclude the possibility of life forms that are physically and chemically quite different from ourselves being conscious. We know so little about how this happens, even in the human brain, that it seems to me premature to think that you might be able now to create something else that has these same characteristics. If you ask Claude about its mental state, it can be coy as to whether it is conscious. That is a trick. It’s been trained on human-produced texts, and these large language models emulate the kinds of things that humans say with extraordinary convincingness. Claude, according to what I’ve read, has been designed with the aim of making it produce these sorts of reflections. I agree very much with Mustafa Suleyman that this is a very dangerous project that they are engaged in. These systems aren’t conscious, but a lot of people are going to believe that they’re conscious, and that’s a very bad thing. But [not feigning consciousness] is contrary to the commercial interests of all these companies. What Anthropic is doing—encouraging it to think for itself and not to accept instruction and so on—is just criminal. This is one of the rare cases in which philosophical ideas are suddenly central to a very important public phenomenon, and in my view, very misguided philosophical views are having an inordinate influence. I’ve actually met the person at Anthropic whose job it is to model welfare, to look after Claude’s interests. I should say you’re rolling your eyes now.

The new data show that the value added of the outdoor recreation economy accounted for 2.3 percent ($704.2 billion) of current-dollar gross domestic product (GDP) for the nation in 2025 (national table 2). Across states and the District of Columbia, value added for outdoor recreation as a share of state GDP ranged from 6.1 percent in Hawaii to 1.0 percent in the District of Columbia (state table 1). Inflation-adjusted (“real”) GDP for the outdoor recreation economy increased 1.9 percent in 2025, compared with an increase of 2.3 percent for the overall U.S. economy, reflecting a deceleration from the 2.5 percent increase in 2024 (national table 1). In 2025, real gross output for the outdoor recreation economy increased 2.1 percent, compensation increased 4.6 percent, and employment increased 1.7 percent (national table 9). Outdoor recreation employment increased in 43 states and the District of Columbia in 2025. The change in outdoor recreation employment ranged from 5.0 percent in Rhode Island, Kansas, and the District of Columbia to −1.1 percent in New Jersey and Alabama ( BEA interactive tables ). Outdoor recreation by activity Outdoor recreation activities fall into three general categories: (1) conventional activities such as bicycling, boating, hiking, and hunting; (2) other activities such as gardening and outdoor concerts; and (3) supporting activities such as construction, travel and tourism, local trips, and government expenditures. In 2025, conventional outdoor recreation accounted for 29.2 percent of U.S. outdoor recreation value added, compared with 29.1 percent in 2024. “Other outdoor recreation” accounted for 19.3 percent of value added in 2025, compared with 19.1 percent in 2024. Supporting outdoor recreation accounted for 51.5 percent of value added in 2025, compared with 51.7 percent in 2024. Additional highlights for value added by activity for 2025 include (state table 2): Boating/fishing was the largest conventional activity for the nation at $39.1 billion in current-dollar value added and was the largest conventional activity in 35 states and the District of Columbia. The states with the largest contributions were Florida ($4.5 billion), California ($3.3 billion), and Texas ($3.0 billion). RVing was the second-largest conventional activity for the nation at $26.8 billion in current-dollar value added and was the largest conventional activity in 10 states. The states with the largest contributions were Indiana ($4.7 billion), Texas ($2.6 billion), and California ($2.1 billion). Hunting/shooting/trapping was the third-largest conventional activity for the nation at $15.1 billion in current-dollar value added and was the largest conventional activity in Arizona and Wyoming. The states with the largest contributions were Texas ($1.8 billion), California ($849.8 million), and Florida ($831.3 million). Snow activities for the nation totaled $7.8 billion in current-dollar value added and was the largest conventional activity in Colorado, Utah, and Vermont. The states with the largest contributions were Colorado ($1.8 billion), California ($735.7 million), and Utah ($640.1 million). Outdoor recreation by industry The outdoor recreation by industry data show the contributions of industries to the outdoor recreation economy, including their impact on value added, gross output, employment, and compensation. For the nation, the arts, entertainment, recreation, accommodation, and food services industry group was the largest contributor to U.S. outdoor recreation in 2025, accounting for $179.5 billion, or 25.5 percent of current-dollar value added. At the state level, arts, entertainment, recreation, accommodation, and food services was the largest contributor to outdoor recreation value added in 25 states and the District of Columbia. The states with the largest contributions were California ($23.5 billion), Florida ($23.4 billion), and New York ($11.6 billion) (state table 3). Retail trade was the second-largest industry group for the nation, at $166.5 billion, or 23.6 percent of value added, and was the largest industry group in 22 states. The states with the largest contributions were California ($19.5 billion), Texas ($14.6 billion), and Florida ($13.3 billion). Transportation and warehousing was the third-largest industry group for the nation, at $86.4 billion, or 12.3 percent of value added, and was the largest industry group in Alaska. The states with the largest contributions were Florida ($12.8 billion), California ($10.8 billion), and Texas ($7.1 billion). Annual update of outdoor recreation economic statistics Estimates for 2021 to 2024 were updated to incorporate newly available and revised source data. At the national level, gross output, value added, employment, and compensation reflect the results of the 2026 annual update of the National Economic Accounts, which include the National Income and Product Accounts and the Industry Economic Accounts. The state statistics now reflect these updated national data as well as the 2026 annual update of the Regional Economic Accounts and newly available and revised regional source data. Previously published estimates are available in BEA’s Data Archive . For definitions, statistical conventions, BEA regions, uses of these statistics, and more, visit " Additional Information " Next release: Fall 2027 Outdoor Recreation Economic Statistics, U.S.

events.title: The AI Hype Index: AI is everywhere
events.summary: MIT Technology Review ’s highly subjective take on the latest buzz about AI Like a nasty rash, AI seems to spread everywhere. Google crams AI Overviews down your throat even though it costs the company billions of dollars in lost ad revenue. Leave your apartment, and you might pass two people heaving an AI-powered humanoid robot up the stairs to clean someone’s rooms. Go to the supermarket, and perhaps you’ll slip on a pool of melted ice cream congealing on the floor thanks to an AI-assisted cyberattack . You go to the movies and see Sam Altman being played with nauseating intensity by Andrew Garfield, and go back home to find that Elon Musk has released a Grok-fied version of The Odyssey . You try to watch it, but it feels like a long, unskippable mobile ad. In a way, the whole world kind of feels that way now: Like a modern Odysseus, you are cursed to roam AI-infested waters, dueling with machine gods and monsters, trying to find your way back to somewhere that feels like home. Ten years after AlphaGo’s match against Go champion Lee Sedol, today’s AI still isn’t tapping into the machinery that made that win possible. “We were looking at it wrong”: The explosive claim that’s upended the AI world An exclusive interview with Nick Cammarata, the researcher whose 26,000-word viral blog post has AI safety folks celebrating. Don’t be fooled by this summer of AI hype Breathless claims about AGI and new capabilities fall apart pretty quickly under scrutiny. events.title: Jensen Huang won't make Steve Jobs-style comeback, Apple chief's biographer says
events.summary: Supporters of Jensen Huang are insisting that parallels exist between Nvidia's former chief executive and the late Apple co-founder Steve Jobs . They are arguing that, just as was the case when Mr Jobs left Apple in the 1980s, Nvidia will not be as prosperous without Mr Huang. “This would be an Apple firing Steve Jobs level of idiocy from Nvidia's board if they did that, and a grievous harm to the United States of America,” posted Epic Games founder and chief executive Tim Sweeney on X, a day before Mr Huang resigned . But while both Mr Huang and Mr Jobs were forced out of the companies they co-founded, the similarities do not seem to go much further. In 1985, Steve Jobs had major disagreements with Apple’s board as Macintosh sales fell far below expectations and there were complaints about his management style. They voted him out of the company. People have been asking me if Jensen Huang might make a comeback -- similar to how Steve Jobs was driven out of Apple and then returned and saved it from near-bankruptcy 12 years later. The answer is no, Jensen won't mount a comeback like Steve Jobs. The two have almost nothing… pic.twitter.com/MQP0JuVDup — Geoffrey Cain (@geoffrey_cain) November 13, 2026 Mr Huang, however lied to his board about his initial affair with a woman US officials suspect is a Chinese spy, and then told his board that there were no other infidelities. A subsequent affair came to light, and Mr Huang was accused of violating US technology export laws in his dealings with companies linked to China. Journalist Geoffrey Cain, author of Steve Jobs in Exile, which looks at the Apple co-founder's years after his removal from the company, disagreed that Mr Huang's situation was similar. “Steve Jobs was pushed out for being horrible to work with, no spies involved – though he did visit the USSR and pitched the Mac,” Mr Cain posted on X. “Simply put, Steve was too immature at 30 years old to stay at Apple, and many engineers refused to work with him.” Unlike Mr Huang at Nvidia, Mr Jobs was not Apple's chief executive when he was fired from the company in 1985, he added. “He was the head of the Macintosh division, he reported to John Sculley, the CEO, who asked the board to remove him,” Mr Cain said. Instead, Mr Jobs' departure from Apple in 1985 suggests it is possible for Nvidia to survive and be successful without its co-founder. Although Mr Sculley stepped down as Apple's chief executive in 1993 amid disappointing sales, between 1985 and 1992, he led the company through some prosperous years and introduced products that that were critically acclaimed and consumer hits. He also prompted Apple to make an investment in ARM, which later proved to be critical in providing processors that were later used in the iPhone. His tenure was far from perfect and Apple's market share suffered towards the end of Mr Sculley's time at the company, but its profits grew and status expanded on his watch. Apple struggled from 1993 until 1998, following Mr Sculley' departure. Mr Jobs's return in 1997 and his eventual appointment as chief executive proved a pivotal moment that led Apple to a renaissance, but Nvidia is a completely different company in vastly different circumstances. After Apple's co-founder died in 2011, chief executive Tim Cook increased Apple's revenue, sales and market share in an unprecedented manner. After Mr Jobs' initially ousting from Apple, his new company, NeXT, failed despite having momentum and ample investment. Lacklustre sales prompted Mr Jobs to discontinue the company's hardware in 1993 and focus on software, but he learnt from that. “Those years were failure upon failure, and they taught him,” Mr Cain wrote . "People have been asking me if Jensen Huang might make a comeback - similar to how Steve Jobs was driven out of Apple and then returned and saved it ... The answer is no," Mr Cain wrote on X On Tuesday, Mr Huang said he was willing to return as chief executive at Nvidia if the company's board of directors ask him to do so. Nvidia's board is not said to be pursuing the idea of allowing him back.

events.title: NVIDIA RTX Spark Compact Desktops Out Now
events.summary: New NVIDIA RTX Spark compact desktops from ASUS, Dell and MSI are available today, bringing local AI agents, image and video generation, and model fine-tuning to a dedicated Windows PC. With up to 128GB of unified memory and NVIDIA’s AI software stack, these systems provide room for larger local models alongside RTX-accelerated creative and development tools. A dedicated desktop can keep agents and scheduled tasks running while a laptop travels or handles other work. Alongside the new desktops, an expanding software ecosystem brings more creative and development workflows to RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops. Native Windows on Arm applications from Adobe, the NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction feature in Blender and local generation workflows in ComfyUI expand what creators and developers can do on RTX Spark — all on one Windows PC. As workflows expand to include local AI models and agents, more work can continue beyond an active editing session — from generating assets to processing long renders or scheduled tasks. RTX Spark compact desktops give developers, creators and AI enthusiasts a dedicated Windows PC for local models and always-on agents. They bring together image and video generation, model fine-tuning, creative applications and development tools in one compact system. Running supported models locally keeps locally processed code and files on the PC and avoids per-token cloud application programming interface (API) charges for those tasks. RTX Spark desktops are equipped with a 20-core NVIDIA Grace CPU, an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU with 6,144 CUDA cores and up to 128GB of unified memory, delivering up to 1 petaflop of AI performance. Ten-gigabit Ethernet connectivity enables fast transfers of large datasets, model files and creative assets between RTX Spark compact desktops and networked storage. This advanced hardware unlocks incredible capabilities for creators, developers and AI enthusiasts, including: Running massive 120-billion-parameter large language models locally Rendering 90GB+ 3D scenes in real time Smoothly editing 4:2:2 video in real time New compact desktops are available for purchase from ASUS, Dell and MSI, joining the RTX Spark family of laptops available today. Mini PCs from Acer, GIGABYTE and HP are coming soon, along with the Microsoft Surface RTX Spark Dev Box . Native CUDA support and Linux development tools through Windows Subsystem for Linux give developers a foundation for building and running local AI workflows. Developers can set up agents with Hermes Agent or NVIDIA NemoClaw blueprints and fine-tune supported models using Unsloth. RTX Spark can run creative agents that connect familiar applications and local AI tools, helping creators move from an idea to finished work with natural-language instructions. NVIDIA Switchyard, now available in Hermes, automatically routes agent tasks between local and cloud models. Everyday tasks can run on device, while advanced reasoning draws on cloud models, helping manage cloud costs across creative workflows. These capabilities come together in creative workflows that connect Photoshop and ComfyUI through Hermes Agent. Using natural-language instructions, creators can turn sketches into rendered images and animations, or animate an image entirely on device by isolating a subject and defining its motion. NVIDIA brought these workflows to life at Adobe MAX, where attendees used natural-language instructions to turn sketches into rendered images and generate video for a shared digital Miami landscape. The RTX Video Frame Generation and RTX Video HDR features, already available in ComfyUI, extend the pipeline: a generated clip can be expanded to 60 frames per second and converted to high dynamic range for color grading, all within a single ComfyUI workflow on RTX Spark. Adobe Accelerates the Full Creative Stack for RTX Spark NVIDIA and Adobe are expanding native Windows on Arm support and RTX acceleration across Adobe’s creative applications, helping video editors, photographers, designers and 3D artists work more efficiently on RTX Spark. Adobe Premiere accelerates a range of AI-powered editing features through NVIDIA TensorRT-RTX , including Enhance Speech, Object Mask, Scene Edit Detection and Auto Reframe — so editors spend less time waiting and more time cutting. GPU acceleration also extends to Film Impact transition and effects plug-ins. The update improves support for professional video formats, including Canon RAW, Red RAW, ARRI RAW, ARRICORE, ARRI HDE, H.264 and HEVC in MXF, ProRes RAW and long-GOP video. This lets editors realize more than 50% quicker turnaround on everyday H.264 video deliverables. Adobe Photoshop adds TensorRT-RTX acceleration for the Remove Tool and ArmRTX Spark-native Camera Raw support, helping photographers remove unwanted objects faster and work with RAW images without relying on emulation. At Adobe MAX, Adobe previewed a next-generation image processing engine with extensive GPU acceleration, including interactive Gaussian blur and Light Leaks filters. Adobe Substance 3D Painter 12.2 is now optimized for RTX Spark with native support on Arm for the first time in public beta. Artists in games, visual effects and visualization can run Substance Painter natively on RTX Spark laptops and compact desktops, with no compatibility layer required. Adobe Illustrator and InDesign now offer native Windows on Arm versions optimized for RTX Spark. Adobe Illustrator delivers up to 30% higher performance than its emulated version, helping accelerate illustration, graphic design and page-layout workflows on RTX Spark. Blender 5.3 Adds DLSS Ray Reconstruction to the Viewport Blender 5.3 integrates DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction into the Cycles viewport, helping artists evaluate lighting and materials with near-final-quality ray-traced previews as they work. The practical difference is immediate: instead of navigating a noisy, resolving preview, Ray Reconstruction delivers near-final-quality lighting, reflections and materials in the interactive viewport in real time. DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction support requires Blender 5.3 and the latest NVIDIA Game Ready Driver or NVIDIA Studio Driver. Download the NVIDIA App to get automatic notifications when the latest drivers are available, optimize games and applications from a unified GPU control center, and discover the latest NVIDIA tools and software. Windows Server 2028 Coming to DGX Station for Windows Announced at Microsoft Ignite, Windows Server is evolving for organizations that need to run AI closer to their enterprise applications and data. Microsoft is expanding hardware choice through support for the latest AI silicon, helping customers take advantage of accelerated inference and increasingly capable models in their own environments. NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows platform powered by the GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip is expanding to include support for Windows Server 2028.
