events.title: IMF puts UAE back into growth territory for 2026
events.summary: The International Monetary Fund has upgraded its projection for the UAE’s economy to 0.2 per cent growth this year, amid the easing of Iran war disruption and a recovery in oil production. The IMF had previously said it would shrink by 3.9 per cent. The change marks a major turnaround for the Arab world's second-largest economy. Real gross domestic product is expected to grow by 7.3 per cent next year, slightly lower than the fund's previous projection of 7.7 per cent, the IMF said after a visit to the UAE this month. “The UAE economy has demonstrated strong resilience to regional disruptions, supported by the authorities’ swift policy response,” Said Bakhache, IMF mission chief for the UAE, said. “Substantial public-sector and external buffers, a well-capitalised banking system and targeted fiscal and financial-sector measures helped cushion the impact.” Oil recovery The fund said oil production had also recovered, while some non-oil sectors were showing signs of gradual recovery, supporting the growth of the UAE economy. The Iran war, in its ninth month, has disrupted a number of sectors across the region, with tourism and aviation among the most affected as airlines cancel or reschedule flights. The Strait of Hormuz, the global chokepoint for crude supply, was effectively shut as Iran attacked ships transiting the channel. Inflation stays high However, regional countries including the UAE and Saudi Arabia began to supply crude to global markets through pipelines as well as via ships. UAE Minister of Energy and Infrastructure Suhail Al Mazrouei told Adipec this month that the country’s oil exports surpassed prewar levels “at a certain time” during the conflict. The non-hydrocarbon sector is projected to contract by 0.5 per cent in 2026 and expand by 5.4 per cent in 2027, while hydrocarbon growth is expected at 2.3 per cent in 2026 and 13.3 per cent in 2027, the IMF said. Inflation is projected to average about 5 per cent in 2026 before easing to about 3 per cent in 2027 and converging towards 2 per cent over the medium term as supply pressures and base effects unwind. “The outlook remains subject to significant uncertainty. Escalation of regional tensions and disruptions to trade, tourism and supply chains could delay the recovery and add to inflationary pressures,” Mr Bakhache said. “Global financial volatility and cybersecurity risks also warrant continued attention. On the upside, faster normalisation of regional conflict and stronger investment and productivity gains, including from AI, could support higher growth.” The UAE's financial system remains resilient, underpinned by substantial capital and liquidity buffers, while asset quality has continued to improve. Against the backdrop of elevated inflation and strong credit growth, continued close monitoring of liquidity and funding conditions, asset quality, and sectoral exposures remain important, the IMF said. Developments in real estate and financial innovation also require sustained supervisory vigilance and regulatory co-ordination to further safeguard stability, it added. Real estate activity has moderated from earlier peaks, with conditions varying across emirates and market segments. 'Capacity to adapt' The IMF emphasised greater trade integration and diversification of trade routes to strengthen resilience against future disruptions. It also welcomed comprehensive economic partnership agreements signed by the UAE to expand trade partnerships. “The resilience of the UAE economy and its high capacity to adapt to global developments and sustain growth embody … the effectiveness of the country’s proactive policies, which have reinforced the pillars of financial and monetary stability and solidified the UAE’s standing as a leading global economic and financial centre,” Khaled Balama, Governor of the Central Bank of the UAE and Governor for the UAE at the IMF, said in a separate statement. Total banking assets surpassed Dh5.815 trillion ($1.57 trillion) by the end of the third quarter of 2026, reflecting the “strength, soundness, and high resilience of the banking system in supporting sustainable economic development”, Mr Balama added.

events.title: Mary Peltola unseats Republican Dan Sullivan in Alaska, extending Democratic wave
events.summary: Former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola has defeated two-term Republican Sen. Dan S. Sullivan , flipping another GOP-held seat in a state President Trump carried comfortably in 2024, the AP projects. Why it matters: Peltola becomes the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Alaska since 2008, extending a historic blue wave in a race marred by controversy. Her victory comes in a state Trump carried by 13 points in 2024, underscoring the extraordinary reach of the Democratic backlash against his second term. It also delivers another blow to Republicans after sweeping Democratic victories in states including Texas, Ohio, Iowa and South Carolina. What they're saying: "As a lifelong Alaskan who has dedicated my career to serving our state, there is no greater honor than having Alaskans' support in our fight to take on corporate greed, lower costs, and put Alaska first," Peltola wrote on X Tuesday evening. "Thank you, Alaska. Let's get to work," she added. State of play: The race drew scrutiny after The New York Times reported allegations that Democratic operatives recruited another candidate named Dan Sullivan to draw votes from the incumbent. Peltola's campaign denied involvement, but the reporting prompted Alaska's Republican governor, Mike Dunleavy, to order an investigation into whether state laws were broken. The Justice Department also launched a criminal investigation and subpoenaed people connected to the alleged effort. No one involved in the race has been charged with a crime. On the campaign trail, the candidates clashed over the cost of living, the Iran war and Alaska's energy industry, with Peltola challenging Sullivan's record in Washington. Peltola campaigned on her signature "fish, family and freedom" message, emphasizing affordability, protecting Alaska's fisheries and putting the state's interests ahead of party politics. Trump traveled to Alaska in October to rally support for Sullivan, whom he praised as one of Washington's most respected senators. Sullivan embraced the president's support , betting it would energize Republican voters despite their party's political headwinds. The big picture: Alaska has long leaned Republican, but Peltola's ability to win crossover support — including votes from Republicans who ranked her above former Gov. Sarah Palin in 2022 — helped put the state in play for Democrats. Peltola made history in that 2022 special election as the first Alaska Native elected to Congress. She won a full term later that year before losing her House seat to Republican Nick Begich in 2024. Sullivan, a former Alaska attorney general and Marine Corps veteran, has represented Alaska in the Senate since 2015. The two-term Republican campaigned on his record on energy development and national security. Context: Another candidate named Dan Sullivan — a retired teacher from Petersburg, Alaska, listed on the ballot as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. — became a factor in the race. The Trump administration sued Alaska on Oct. 22, seeking to delay certification if Sen. Sullivan lost and votes for the other Dan Sullivan could have changed the outcome. A federal judge dismissed the lawsuit on Nov. 1, ruling that the administration lacked standing to bring the case and that its proposed remedy was unworkable. The Justice Department appealed the decision. Sen. Sullivan committed to accepting the results even if he didn't win. How it works: Alaska's ranked-choice voting system added another wrinkle. Voters rank candidates in order of preference. If no candidate wins a majority of first-choice votes, the last-place candidate is eliminated and votes for that candidate are redistributed according to voters' next available choices. The process repeats until a candidate wins a majority. What's next: Alaska election officials will complete the remaining certification steps, with the Justice Department's appeal potentially affecting the process.

events.title: Highlights from my opening of the Ignite keynote this morning on how we’re building a frontier ecosystem to turn advances in AI into real-world impact.
events.summary: People stopped being impressed by AI demos, they just want their work to get easier. ⠀ Microsoft talking about an ecosystem instead of a single model is how that actually happens. Exciting to see GPT-6.2 and Meta's models coming to Foundry, giving businesses more flexibility to build AI solutions around their specific needs. Satya Nadella Opening by owning last week’s outage was the strongest moment of the keynote for me. Customers forgive a bad day. What they remember is how you talk about it the morning after, and take accountability. As AI takes on more of the real work, that kind of candor will matter as much as any model Well said, Sir. A frontier ecosystem only matters when it works on the ground, not just on stage. In my daily work on data centres, I see this gap clearly. AI can show great promise in a demo, but real-world impact comes when power, cooling, connectivity and resilience all hold together under continuous load. When an AI system has to act, decide and execute, there is no room for downtime or latency. That is why this shift from models to real outcomes is so important. The value will not come from how advanced the model is alone, but from how reliably the infrastructure behind it can support it at scale, across different regions, languages and operating conditions like we have in India. Building that dependable layer is what will turn AI advances into actual productivity, and that is where the real work lies. The one thing that struck while looking on this morning was how Microsoft was making itself a one stop shop to better compete. On a micro level, I created an AI Productivity and Workforce Transformation Programme™ with the intent to improve work processes and bridge the gap for those who can't pay or are not as knowledge using AI tools. As such it is also beginner friendly. I have about twelve tools in my Programme that also includes Microsoft Copilot, Excel AI, Word and Microsoft Forms. Looking at the presentation, I was amazed how Microsoft is competing with the Zapier's, Otter AI, Trello, Notion and others - kind of made me feel like I should rewrite the Programne using only Microsoft tools. However, that won't help many because my Programme tells people how to get things done using free AI tools until they can pay/ upgrade to the paid tools for greater, better results and collaboration. I was impressed by Microsoft's presentation today though👍🏼 As Microsoft moves toward more autonomous AI agents, how do you envision measuring success beyond adoption and productivity? Could business outcomes become the primary measure of AI’s value? Keeping Humans at the centre. Human in the Room. Human in the Loop. Satya, appreciate the company's transparency initiatives. Also appreciate MSFT's efforts to integrate Copilot into its products or your own ecosystem to bring efficiency. However, how about prioritizing the use of AI LLMs to make MS Office (and Windows in general) more efficient, less bloated, and, more importantly, a bit more self-aware? Even today, while active on Teams for a meeting, it will ask me to authenticate myself/my account while i attempt to open an MS office document from the meeting. The desktop version of Outlook struggles to synchronize accounts unless they are outlook/msn accounts. I hope MSFT will surprise us with these improvements soon! CHeers and good luck The most consequential takeaway from the keynote isn’t just Copilot evolving into an OS for work-it’s the architectural emphasis on enterprises owning their context layer (Microsoft IQ), tracking unit economics via Agent 365, and enforcing runtime containment through Microsoft Perception and Execution Containers. Scaling autonomous agents in production only works when context governance, FinOps telemetry, and non-human identity boundaries are built into the stack from day one. The move from single-player AI to people working alongside agents is where most mid-size organizations in Latin America will feel Ignite's impact. What we see on the ground is that the technology arrives before the groundwork: identity, permissions and data classification decide whether agents create value or create risk. I'm curious how much of this ecosystem will make that groundwork easier for companies without large security teams. My annual letter: Building the frontier ecosystem Satya Nadella 1mo The Infinite SaaS Factory Satya Nadella 1mo How do we build a frontier intelligence ecosystem? events.title: Attackers Used Optimizely to A/B Test Malware on Top Websites
events.summary: At least 178 top web destinations unwittingly served a variety of malware exploits against visitors over the past 24 hours thanks to a security vulnerability involving Optimizely , a company that helps websites customize user experiences and test out new features. Experts say the incident, which saw data-stealing malicious software silently injected into sites like the BBC , CNN , Equifax , Ledger and Zoom , was exacerbated by the reality that few popular websites enforce strict rules on the sources of third-party content. The Zoom.com homepage loading the malicious JavaScript file from Optimizely. Image: blog.report-uri.com. Click to enlarge. According to a blog post from the security firm Report URI , on November 16 malicious JavaScript code was served to visitors of 178 organizations through Optimizely’s platform. Report URI researcher Scott Helme wrote that the payload delivered by the malicious Javascript was rebuilt 26 times during the day, dropping a multi-purpose malware kit that could steal payment card data, cookies and screenshots, and swap any cryptocurrency payment addresses for the attacker’s. Helme noted the affected websites also served exploit code custom made to attack known vulnerabilities in older Apple iPhone and iPad devices. Known by such names as “ DarkSword ” and “ Coruna ,” these are zero-click exploit kits that chain together a half-dozen security holes to seize complete control over outdated devices and extract data. “The important lesson here is that trusted JavaScript doesn’t always remain trustworthy,” Helme wrote . “A website can be compromised through a third-party dependency without its own code or infrastructure ever being breached.” Contacted for comment, Optimizely said that on November 16, 2026 it “identified a security incident in which an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in the Optimizely Experimentation to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects.” “We acted swiftly to contain the incident and have fully remediated the identified vulnerability,” reads a written statement shared by Optimizely. “These measures included blocking access to the vulnerable path, deploying a fix, removing the injected code from affected projects, ending active sessions, revoking tokens, and resetting access for affected user accounts. We have also implemented additional protections to prevent malicious code from being delivered in Cloudflare. While the incident has been fully remediated, we are working with third-party experts on a comprehensive investigation.” Many top web properties no longer fully display content unless visitors agree to let often dozens of third parties serve JavaScript, a powerful web scripting language that enables interactive content. JavaScript code is run on the user’s device, and it can read information displayed in the user’s browser and even modify a website’s appearance or content. One reason JavaScript is so heavily used is that it enables fairly precise browser fingerprinting and other ways of tracking visitors and clicks. According to the 2025 Web Almanac by HTTP Archive, the median homepage loads at least 22 JavaScript files. But as the incident with Optimizely shows, a compromise at a third-party vendor’s website can quickly snowball into a supply chain attack against downstream websites that end up serving visitors tampered and malicious JavaScript files. Zach Edwards is a researcher at Infoblox and the co-founder of the ad-tracking service DecryptAds . Edwards said Optimizely is a vendor which often collects data outside of consent flows, with their JavaScript snippets being embedded as close to the top of the page as possible to ensure that it’s one of the first things to render, which is important since the product is primarily built for A/B testing. “So to make the product work as expected, this code is setup to fire immediately on-page load, and not restrict rendering behind a consent dialog box,” he said. “This means that this supply chain attack didn’t require any clicking or consent to trigger — most of the impacted clients would immediately serve up the payload as soon as someone loaded the page, further increasing risks from this type of JavaScript snippet being compromised.” Websites can minimize the chances that a breach at a third-party content provider spirals into a supply chain attack by taking full advantage of “ Content Security Policies ” or CSPs, which specify the domain names that are allowed to serve third-party content. But Edwards said most websites — apart from perhaps the largest e-commerce, social media and financial platforms — don’t even bother with CSPs, or else tend to leave them overly permissive for marketing reasons. “With literally all websites which embed 3rd party JavaScript resources, if you don’t have a content security policy then if any of those partners get compromised, new domains can be injected into your website via JavaScript which won’t be stopped,” he said. “We’re in the age of JavaScript supply chain attacks and yet almost no one is talking about why content security policies were invented and how this is largely the solution for operators, even though it’s not always simple to get it initially deployed.” How broadly deployed were CSPs at the websites impacted by the Optimizely attack? According to Report URI, 68 of the sites had no CSP at all, while 50 of them had a CSP that still allowed the malware payload and the data theft. The company found only 24 of the affected sites (15 percent) had CSPs that fully blocked the malicious payload. Image: blog.report-uri.com. The overall deployment of CSPs across the Web’s busiest sites is somewhat lower — about 10 percent — according to Helme’s site crawler.ninja , which scans the top million websites daily for security issues. Helme said he hopes this incident will encourage more sites to adopt effective CSPs, noting that it could have been far worse: By Report URI’s estimates, the purveyors of this malware attack managed to steal only around $7,500 worth of virtual currency from affected users, as well as an unknown number of payment card records. Helme said he often compares the current widespread lack of CSPs to the Wild West. “Organizations are running all this code, but they don’t know what it’s doing,” Helme said in an interview with KrebsOnSecurity. “This is why we keep seeing such large scale breaches in places [where] there are no checks and rules in place on the code we’re running, so this was kind of inevitable. events.title: Some Nvidia directors continue push to bring Huang back
events.summary: Despite Nvidia’s proclamation Tuesday that it didn’t plan to bring ousted CEO Jensen Huang back to the chipmaker, a faction of board members is pushing for his return, according to people familiar with the matter. Huang has met with a number of tech executives and spoken with at least one board member about the possibility of his return, the people said. The conversation with the director took place before the company’s earnings report and before Huang issued a public statement Tuesday that he’d be willing to return to the company if the board decides it is in the “best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America.” Hours later, Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said on the company’s earnings call that the chipmaker wasn’t considering bringing Huang back and that the board had voted unanimously to accept his resignation. Spokespeople for Huang and Nvidia declined to comment. Despite the pushback from three directors, other board members are starting to narrow the search for Huang’s replacement, some of the people familiar with the deliberations said. ARM CEO Rene Haas and Marvell CEO Matt Murphy have both been considered, the people said. Haas has spoken to at least some Nvidia directors about taking the job, one of the people said, but he’s said he’s concerned about the optics of taking it over calls to bring Huang back to the helm. Spokespeople for ARM and Marvell didn’t immediately respond to requests for comment. It’s also unclear whether Marvell’s Murphy would be able to take over as Nvidia’s CEO given the company is navigating a mega-merger with rival Lumentum.
